newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge nosedives on earnings jitters.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge nosedives on earnings jitters.

text.p: Selling battered shares in networking equipment company Newbridge Networks Corp as investors grew concerned about the end of Newbridge's second quarter on October 30.
Newbridge shares tumbled 4.50 to 40.50 in heavy volume of 1.56 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange and relinquished 3-3/8 to 30-1/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Fears about Newbridge's quarters often send tremors through its share price. Newbridge is due to report its second quarter on November 19.
But this time the downward pressure has been increased by speculation that rival Cascade Communications Corp may poised to grab business from some of Newbridge's major clients, analysts said.
Cascade recently introduced a multimedia switch which directly competes with Newbridge's flagship 36170.

"This time it looks like you have to combine a back-end loaded quarter with the thought that Cascade may have caused a couple of RBOCs (regional Bell operating companies) to delay or at least pause before making purchasing 36170s," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
"This is all speculation, of course," the analyst added.
A back-end loaded quarter is one wherein more than one-third of sales occur in the last month of a three-month earnings period.
Dillon Read & Co technology analyst Robert MacLellan said this type of quarter is very common for companies in the networking sector, and he is maintaining a buy on the stock.
"(The fall is due to) normal general nervousness about the firm making the quarter. Plus you have had a sell-off in the high-tech sector for the last couple of days," MacLellan said.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.coms
